verdict.rationale: Ramp's own docs describe Funds as budgets with amount, interval and merchant restrictions. Its spend controls apply to cards, reimbursements and bills, enforce limits before spend happens, and route approvals by amount, with recommendations grounded in budgets. Team-scoped cards are documented, but project-level budget allocation is not, and all evidence is vendor-claimed. missing for 10: explicit documentation of allocating budgets to projects (and team-level budget hierarchies), independent or hands-on corroboration that limits and approvals actually block over-budget spend.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can allocate budgets to teams and projects and have card limits and approvals actually enforce them

citations.quote: Funds. A budget with restrictions — amount, interval (daily, monthly, total), allowed merchant categories, allowed merchants, allowed countries.
The policy layer behind every dollar spent on Ramp — budgets, templates, and approval workflows that apply equally to cards, reimbursements, bills, and agent purchases.
Set submission requirements, enforce spend limits, and block risky merchants or categories all before spend happens.
All spend requests come with a recommended action grounded in your policies, budgets, and funds, so you can approve or reject in seconds.
Create custom virtual cards and set permissions for everything from ad marketplace spend to remote work stipends, for individual teams or your whole company.
Rules-based workflows route requests to the right stakeholders automatically based on vendor type, spend category, or dollar amount
